checks.context: QLDB uses an AWS-owned key by default. For ledgers storing financial or compliance data, specify --kms-key with a CMK ARN so you have an audit trail of every access and can revoke access independently. Note: QLDB is deprecated (end of life July 2025) — migrate to other services.

checks.message: QLDB ledger deletion destroys the entire immutable transaction history
checks.context: The audit log is QLDB's entire value. Export the journal to S3 before deleting if you need to retain the history for compliance.

checks.message: Verify the instance is not being made publicly accessible or moved to a public subnet
checks.context: DocumentDB instances should remain in private subnets. Making them publicly accessible exposes your document database to internet-based attacks.

checks.message: Verify you are not disabling deletion protection or audit logging
checks.context: Disabling deletion protection on a production Neptune cluster exposes it to accidental deletion. Disabling audit logs removes visibility into graph queries and access patterns.

checks.message: Parameter changes may weaken audit logging or security settings
checks.context: Modifying parameters like neptune_enforce_ssl or audit log settings affects all clusters using this parameter group. Disabling SSL enforcement allows unencrypted connections to your graph database.

checks.message: Verify the instance class change doesn't cause performance degradation during modification
checks.context: Instance class changes trigger a brief failover. If modifying the writer instance, all write operations fail during the switchover. Schedule changes during maintenance windows.
